matchup.raw_text: a grizzly bear vs 4 gray wolves in a forest

mass_kg.note: Coastal Alaskan males; low is the northern interior Canada male figure, 139 kg, in the next sentence. The source gives one male figure per population and no overall mean or typical figure, so value is the upper quoted figure (D-47 rule 4 fallback; rechecked in #166).

source.title: Grizzly bear
source.quote: Average total length in this subspecies is between 198 cm (78 in) and 240 cm (94 in)

size_m.note: Total length; the source does not say whether it is male-only. Upper end of the stated range; the source gives no mean.

source.title: Grizzly bear
source.quote: the maximum speed reliably recorded at Yellowstone is 48 km/h (30 mph)

top_speed_mps.note: Converted from 48 km/h; range is the standard +/-10%.

source.title: Bite club: comparative bite force in big biting mammals and the prediction of predatory behaviour in fossil taxa
source.license: Publisher copyright, not an open license; one data row cited

attack_force_n.note: Canine bite force for Ursus arctos, of which the grizzly is a subspecies, estimated from a skull of a 128.8 kg bear, so it likely runs low; range is +/-25%. Rechecked in #166: no better-sourced bite figure exists among the approved sources, so 751 N stays.

attacks_per_s.note: No published attack rate found for this animal; category default.

reach_m.note: reach = 0.25 x size_m (lunging bite), from size_m.

armor_0_1.note: armor level 2: thick fur and fat.

endurance_s.note: No published figure for how long it can keep fighting; category default.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 4: territorial, confident against most animals.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 1: solitary, fights alone.

source.title: Wolf
source.quote: The mean body mass of the wolf is 40 kg (88 lb)

mass_kg.note: Mean for wolves generally, not male-only. Low is the Indian and Arabian wolf average; high is where the source says wolves become uncommon.

source.title: Wolf
source.quote: Adult wolves measure 105–160 cm (41–63 in) in length

size_m.note: The source does not split by sex and lists the tail separately right after. Upper end of the stated range; the source gives no mean.

source.title: Hunting behavior of gray wolves
source.quote: Wolves can run at 56–64 km/h (35–40 mph) across several kilometers

top_speed_mps.note: Converted from 64 km/h, low from 56 km/h.

source.title: Bite club: comparative bite force in big biting mammals and the prediction of predatory behaviour in fossil taxa
source.license: Publisher copyright, not an open license; one data row cited

attack_force_n.note: Canine bite force estimated from a skull of a 34.7 kg wolf; range is +/-25%.

attacks_per_s.note: No published attack rate found for this animal; category default.

reach_m.note: reach = 0.25 x size_m (lunging bite), from size_m.

endurance_s.note: Category default (mammal). Wolves 'can maintain rapid pursuit for at least 20 minutes' (Hunting behavior of gray wolves), but that is a chase minimum, not fighting endurance.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 3: hunts or defends itself, avoids risky fights.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 4: pack that hunts in coordination.

result.deciding_factor_explainer: Gray wolf came out ahead in spite of its size: Gray wolf (40 kg) against Grizzly bear (389 kg).

fair_fight.message: This fight is already about even: 1 grizzly bear against 4 gray wolves.

challenger.reason: Gorilla would be a coin flip against 4 gray wolves.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN! WELCOME TO THE ARENA!

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: Tonight’s matchup features a solitary Grizzly bear against four Gray wolves.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: IN THE RED CORNER, THE MAMMOTH OF MASS: A 389 KILO GRIZZLY BEAR!

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: The simulation indicates its sheer mass is the deciding factor in this encounter.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: IN THE BLUE CORNER, THE PACK PRECISION: FOUR SWIFT 40 KILO WOLVES!

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: They boast superior teamwork and speed to challenge the heavyweight champion.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: THE COMPUTER HAS SPOKEN. LET THE BRAWL BEGIN!

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: The Grizzly bear and the pack close in for battle.

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: Teeth clash immediately as both sides engage contact.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: Four wolves overwhelm the bear with relentless strikes.

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: One wolf goes down, but the pack holds strong.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: The bear breaks off, retreating from the swarm.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: The Grizzly bear is knocked down. The fight ends.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: The decision is in. Your winner: Gray wolf!

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: They took it 55% of the time across all simulations.

lines.speaker: announcer
lines.text: It came down to sheer mass. Total dominance.

lines.speaker: color_commentator
lines.text: Want a fair fight? It's already about even, winning 49% of the time.
